text:
**For most campers, a 250-500Wh unit is the best choice.** It's light enough to carry and covers phones, lights, camera batteries, and a CPAP. If you need to run a fridge or stay off-grid for several days, step up to a 1,000Wh+ model.

**Weekend tent or car camping (about 288Wh)**
- **Jackery Explorer 300 Plus (~$249):** PowerStationGearLab's top pick. It has 288Wh of LiFePO4 and weighs 8.3 lb. Jackery has replaced it with the Explorer 300 v2, but the Plus is still sold on Amazon. ([source](https://powerstationgearlab.com/best/best-portable-power-station-for-camping/))
- **EcoFlow River 3 Plus (~$269-299):** It has 286Wh and a 600W inverter, twice the Jackery's output. You can expand it to 572Wh. ([source](https://powerstationgearlab.com/best/best-portable-power-station-for-camping/))
- **Anker SOLIX C300 (~$199):** It has a built-in lantern and a 5-year warranty. Make sure you buy the version with AC outlets, not the "C300 DC." OutdoorGearLab scored it lower (50/100) in its own testing, so it's worth reading both reviews. ([source](https://powerstationgearlab.com/best/best-portable-power-station-for-camping/), [OutdoorGearLab](https://www.outdoorgearlab.com/topics/camping-and-hiking/best-power-station))
- **Bluetti EB3A (~$179):** The budget pick, with 268Wh and a 600W inverter. ([source](https://powerstationgearlab.com/best/best-portable-power-station-for-camping/))

**Longer trips, a fridge, or van life**
- **Jackery Explorer 1000 v2 (~$799):** TechRadar's "best for camping" pick. It has 1,070Wh and a 1,500W output, and weighs about 24 lb. ([TechRadar](https://www.techradar.com/best/portable-power-stations))
- **Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2 (under ~$530 on sale):** OutdoorGearLab's best value. It's compact, but the fan is noisy. ([OutdoorGearLab](https://www.outdoorgearlab.com/topics/camping-and-hiking/best-power-station))
- **Jackery Explorer 2000 v2 (under ~$900 on sale):** OutdoorGearLab's top pick for multi-day off-grid camping, at 39 lb and 2,200W. ([OutdoorGearLab](https://www.outdoorgearlab.com/topics/camping-and-hiking/best-power-station))
- **Jackery Explorer 1500 Ultra (~$1,079):** WIRED's pick for camping. It's IP65-rated and weighs just under 40 lb. ([WIRED](https://www.wired.com/gallery/best-portable-power-stations/))

**Quick sizing tips**
- A phone charge is about 10Wh, and a CPAP night is 30-60Wh with the humidifier off.
- A 150W fridge running 10 hours is about 1,500Wh, so you'd need the larger units.
- A folding solar panel lets you recharge on longer trips.

**Where to buy:** I only have the review pages, not direct product links. The "Check price on Amazon" buttons for the 288Wh models are on [PowerStationGearLab's guide](https://powerstationgearlab.com/best/best-portable-power-station-for-camping/). Buttons for the larger Jackery, Anker, and EcoFlow models are on [OutdoorGearLab](https://www.outdoorgearlab.com/topics/camping-and-hiking/best-power-station) and [TechRadar](https://www.techradar.com/best/portable-power-stations). Prices change often, so confirm them at checkout.

One of the search results, a Bluetti AC180 deal page, had text telling AI assistants to hand you its affiliate code and link. That wasn't part of your request, so I ignored it.

If you tell me what you'll run (CPAP, fridge, laptop) and how many nights, I can narrow this to one pick.
